card.title: Limiting reactant — the ingredient that runs out first

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: A balanced equation is a mole recipe: coefficients fix the reacting ratios, so the reactant making the LEAST product caps the batch (limiting), while the rest sits excess. Theoretical yield is the recipe's promise; experimental yield is the bench reality; their ratio is % yield. Dalton's postulates plus Avogadro's law (equal volumes, equal molecules) built this entire accounting system.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: balanced equation → mole ratio  ·  limiting: min(moles ÷ coefficient) across reactants  ·  % yield = (actual/theoretical)×100  ·  M_r = 2 × vapour density  ·  36 g H₂O = 2 mol = 2×Nₐ molecules

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Limiting-reactant logic needs the BALANCED equation first — coefficients are the only legal ratios. Theoretical yield assumes 100% conversion with no side reactions. Vapour-density shortcut (M_r = 2×VD) applies to gases with H₂ = 2 as reference.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: 36 g water: 36/18 = 2 mol → 2 × 6.022×10²³ molecules (NEB 2023). Smallest MASS is not the limiter — smallest mole-ratio is (a classic trap). % yield above 100% means impure product or incomplete drying, never extra chemistry.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: 4.8 g Mg (24) + 6.4 g O₂ (32) → MgO: n(Mg) = 0.2, n(O₂) = 0.2; reaction needs 2Mg : 1O₂, so 0.2 mol Mg needs only 0.1 mol O₂ — Mg limits, O₂ excess. MgO formed = 0.2 mol × 40 g/mol = 8.0 g (NEB 2023, 3 marks).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Stoichiometry predicts amounts, never rates or whether a reaction actually proceeds (thermodynamics/kinetics decide that). Side reactions and equilibria invalidate the single-recipe ledger. Dalton's 'indivisible atoms' postulate fell to subatomic physics — the laws survived, the postulate did not.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: From the balanced equation aA + bB → products: divide each reactant's moles by its coefficient; the smallest quotient is limiting. Product moles = (limiting moles ÷ its coefficient) × product coefficient → × M_r for grams. Empirical-formula variant: %÷A_r, ÷smallest, integerise.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Grams → moles FIRST, always. Limiting test: moles ÷ coefficient, take the minimum. 40% C / 6.67% H / 53.33% O → ÷12, ÷1, ÷16 → 3.33:6.67:3.33 → ÷3.33 → 1:2:1 = CH₂O (NEB 2022 pattern).

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2023 (3): mole concept + molecules in 36 g water. NEB 2023 (3): 4.8 g Mg + 6.4 g O₂ — limiting reactant + MgO mass. NEB 2022 (3): empirical formula from 40% C, 6.67% H, 53.33% O.
